Nine comments

An enjoyable fast-moving hornpipe played in sessions in Bristol.
The version posted is “bare bones”. The version in O’Neill’s Dance Music of Ireland (#952), with phrasing, is as follows:

Re: The Sunshine / St. Elmo / Shunster’s

At least two listings in Ryan’s MC as St Elmo (#767) and Shunster’s (#791). They are almost identical settings.

↳ Posted by brailsford on August 24th, 2023.

Re: The Sunshine

Also in S. Howe’s 1000 Jigs and Reels page 55 (1867) as The Shunter, presumably in reference to a railwayman’s job or a dance named after the job of moving railcars.

Shunster and Sunshine must be names non-railwaymen people later derived from the original name Shunter. St. Elmo’s sounds like a lively dance move…

↳ Posted by RJH on January 31st, 2024.

Re: The Sunshine / The Pansy Blossom

The Pansy Blossom is title for O’Neill’s setting in his Music of Ireland (1850) #1667. It differs somewhat from Ryan’s settings but it obviously the same hornpipe.

↳ Posted by brailsford on February 5th, 2024.
